Store Layouts

zarrcurator diagnoses, splits and archives zarr stores in all of these layouts, and creates Kerchunk references for the resulting tarballs:

Layout

Supported

zarr v2 and zarr v3

yes

Chunk key separators . and /

yes: v2 0.1 / 0/1, v3 c.0.1 / c/0/1, and v3 with the v2 key encoding

Nested groups (e.g. written with xarray.DataTree.to_zarr)

yes

Sharded arrays (zarr v3 sharding_indexed)

yes, see Sharding below

A store must open with xarray: every array needs dimension names (_ARRAY_DIMENSIONS in zarr v2, dimension_names in zarr v3). Stores written with xarray have them; stores written with plain zarr may not. dispatchStoreToTarStores checks this first (with checkStoreOpensWithXarray) and raises a ValueError before diagnosing, splitting or archiving a store xarray cannot open.

Nested groups

In a store with nested groups, each array is handled by its path from the store root, e.g. atmos/ocean/salinity.

  • Diagnosis records the size of each array by its path, and the metadata files of each group, e.g. atmos/.zgroup (v2) or atmos/zarr.json (v3).

  • findMissingChunksInStore checks every array in the store, including those in nested groups. The .check report is keyed by the array path, e.g. /atmos/ocean/salinity.

  • Splitting: a group whose arrays together fit the target size goes into one tarball. A larger group is split into its arrays and its sub groups, which are handled the same way; an array larger than the target is split into tarballs of its chunks.

  • Coordinates: each tarball gets the coordinate variables of its arrays. A group can use the coordinates of the groups above it, as in an xarray DataTree, so each coordinate is looked up in the array’s own group first, then in its parent groups up to the store root.

  • Tarballs contain the metadata of every group from the store root down to their arrays, so each tarball opens with xarray.open_datatree.

Sharding

In a sharded array each shard is one file, so zarrcurator handles shards like chunks:

  • findMissingChunksInStore checks the shards (expected_chunks counts shards). A shard of zero size is reported under zero_size; zarr reads an empty shard as not written, so unlike a zero-size chunk it is not also reported as corrupt.

  • Arrays larger than the target size are split into tarballs of whole shards. A shard cannot be split, so a single shard larger than the target size makes a tarball larger than the target.

  • The Kerchunk references point to the inner chunks: the index of each shard is read from the tarball (at the end or the start of the shard, its crc32c checksum verified) and each inner chunk becomes a reference to its byte range. A corrupted shard index raises a ValueError.

Nested sharding, a codec applied after sharding_indexed, and shard index codecs other than bytes with an optional crc32c are not supported and raise a ValueError.

Kerchunk references

createKerchunkReferenceFileForTar writes the references of one tarball; convertKerchunkReferenceFilesOfZarrStoreToParquet merges the references of all tarballs of a store (<store>_*_Offset_kerchunk.json) into one parquet reference of the whole store (<store>.parq).

  • The tarballs of a store are parts of it, so their references are merged: each chunk of a data variable is in one tarball; metadata and coordinate variables are in several and are kept once, after checking that their content is the same. A key with a different content in two tarballs raises a ValueError.

  • The references are written in the zarr v2 layout. For zarr v3 stores the metadata is translated to zarr v2 and the chunks are referenced unchanged, which works for the bytes codec followed by at most one compressor (zstd, gzip, blosc or a numcodecs.* codec). The reopened data is zarr v2.

  • The references of different stores are not combined: tarballs are not concatenated along time.

Opening the references of a store without nested groups:

import fsspec
import xarray as xr

mapper = fsspec.get_mapper(
    "reference://", fo="work/mystore.parq", remote_protocol="file"
)
ds = xr.open_dataset(mapper, engine="zarr", consolidated=False, zarr_format=2)

Opening the references of a store with nested groups needs consolidated=True, as fsspec’s listing of parquet references does not find nested groups:

tree = xr.open_datatree(
    "reference://",
    engine="zarr",
    consolidated=True,
    zarr_format=2,
    storage_options={"fo": "work/mystore.parq", "remote_protocol": "file"},
)

Synthetic test stores

python -m zarrcurator.synthetic_store generates small stores in each of these layouts, with anomalies injected for the diagnostics, see the README. The fixture in tests/data/synthetic_experiment holds one store per layout and frequency.
